newsitem.title: USA: Air Force to resume recovery of crashed A-10.
newsitem.headline: Air Force to resume recovery of crashed A-10.

text.p: The Air Force said on Wednesday it will resume efforts in Colorado next week to recover the wreckage of an A-10 attack jet and the remains of Capt. Craig Button, who disappeared mysteriously in the aircraft two months ago.
The wreckage of Button's fighter was found on April 20 on a Rocky Mountain peak after the aircraft, which was loaded with bombs, disappeared on April 2.

Fragmentary human remains were recovered from the snow-covered wreckage at the time and the Air Force said they had been identified as those of Button by using DNA testing by scientists at the Armed Forces Institute of Pathology in Washington.

The A-10 warplane disappeared during a routine training mission and Air Force officials have been at a loss to explain why Button veered northeast into Colorado, some 850 miles (1,360 km) away from a training exercise in Arizona.
The Air Force said recovery operations, hindered earlier by heavy snow and rugged terrain, would resume on July 7.

"The main purpose of this operation is to recover weapons, flares, ejection seat pyrotechnics, the pilot's remains and other materials useful to the Accident Investigation Board," the service said in a statement.

Button, whose plane was carrying four 500-pound (225-kg) bombs, broke formation after leaving Davis-Monthan Air Force Base near Tucson, Arizona, headed for the Barry M. Goldwater Bombing Range in Arizona.
